title: Track session content labels and host-controlled releases
summary: Grants gain optional clearances; a grant without them clears no labels, so existing hosts keep working for unlabelled sessions, whose journals, state and model requests keep their 3.5 shape. All session hand-overs enforce current root-profile authority and accumulated content labels, including retries and no-work advances. Hosts can label operation results and replies, enforce labels atomically through admission, and authorize deterministic releases whose cleared output crosses a boundary without exposing private session history. Journal replay and runner evidence preserve labels and release provenance. Labelled content and releases are journalled as event version 3, which 3.5 readers refuse: upgrade readers before writers that label. Session, run, attempt, question and receipt types gain a required label (and sessions their releases), so code that builds those values itself must add them. The runner returns every session through the engine's disclosure check, reports a failing host authorization as the redacted IA-ENGINE-AUTHORITY-DENIED, and never clears a label.
